Why bother

A small errand costs more than it looks

Find the address someone sent this morning. Move a file from mail into an editor. Then dig up the wording you already wrote once and cannot quite remember. Each errand costs seconds, and each one makes you leave the document, hunt for a window and come back.

Impuls keeps those things on one surface above the window you are in: clipboard history, a shelf for files, snippets and notes. Instead of switching applications, you pull the panel down, take what you need and carry on from the same place.

Actions

One search across clipboard, snippets and notes

Clipboard history, snippets and notes answer the same query. You do not have to remember which one you put it in.

Modules

Nine modules, one rail

The rails either side of the cutout hold nine module icons, and all nine are there for the same reason: a small job not worth leaving the window for. Anything that fails that test stays out of the rail. You can switch any module off or reorder it in Settings. Actions and Battery have their own sections above and below; the rest are here.

File shelf

Drop a file on the panel, switch to another application and pick it up there. The original never moves: the shelf holds a reference, not a copy.

The local Apple Vision tools live here too — recognise text, remove a background, change format, scale down, build a PDF from several images. Every result is a new file beside the original, and the last operation can be undone.

Clipboard history

What you copied an hour ago is still there. Impuls tells text, links, addresses, phone numbers, colours, JSON, code, files and images apart, and labels the type of every entry.

Pin what matters and it outlives the retention limit. Monitoring pauses, chosen applications are excluded, and concealed password-manager entries never enter the history at all.

Snippets

The text you write over and over: an address, account details, a command, a standing call link. Give each one a short name and find it by that.

Snippets also answer searches in Actions, so remembering where a particular piece of text lives is optional.

Notes

Somewhere to put a thought that matters for an hour: a number from a call, half a link, an idea. A note is created empty and instantly, and empty ones clear themselves away.

It is not a text editor: no folders, no formatting, no search inside the module. It holds the draft that would otherwise live in an unsaved tab.

Translate

The macOS translator inside the panel. The language is chosen in each column's heading, and the direction is read from the script of the text you typed.

Every language the system translator knows is available. When a language pack is missing or a pair is impossible, the menu says so in advance — that option is greyed out rather than hidden.

Music

The source is chosen explicitly. Apple Music is read natively through its scripting interface; Yandex Music, VK Music and YouTube Music open their own official sites in a system WebKit window.

Choosing a source makes no request — the connection appears only after Open Web Player. Instead of a blanket “nothing is playing”, the panel names the reason: the application is not open, no track is running, or permission is needed.

Swipe the capture to see the whole panel

That leaves Calendar: the next meeting, how long until it starts, and a join button when the invitation carries a link. Calendar access is requested by the standard macOS dialog and is needed by this module alone.

Devices

Power

The charge of your Mac and everything attached to it.

Mac, AirPods, iPhone and iPad in one tab, without a separate utility. Impuls shows what the system reports and nothing more: a value it cannot read stays unavailable rather than turning into a zero or a guess.

Swipe the capture to see the whole panel

  • MacCharge, power state, time to empty or to full, plus capacity, voltage, temperature and cycle count wherever macOS publishes them. On desktop Macs the module is called Power.
  • AirPods and accessoriesFrom the values macOS exposes itself. Availability depends on the model and on what the system knows at that moment.
  • iPhone and iPad — BetaThrough the trust the device has already given this Mac: over the cable, or through Finder Wi-Fi sync. Impuls pairs nothing, scans no network and opens no direct connection to the device.
  • Off until you turn it onDevice discovery is a single switch in Settings. While it is off, Impuls opens no connection and reads nothing. Raw device identifiers are never shown, logged or written into a backup.

Behaviour

On every screen

The built-in display, an external monitor, an iPad running as a Sidecar display. The panel opens wherever the pointer is, and folds back into the edge when it is no longer wanted.

  • Displays

    On every screen

    The built-in display with a cutout, an external monitor, an iPad running as a Sidecar display. The panel opens on whichever screen the pointer is on, and only ever one is expanded — carrying the same data.

  • No cutout needed

    Not only MacBooks

    On a MacBook the panel uses the cutout's own geometry. On a screen without one, Impuls draws a compact black anchor of 120 × 12 pt at the top edge; the menu bar either side of it behaves exactly as before.

  • Opening

    Hover or a shortcut

    The activation mode, the hover delay and the key combination are all set in Settings. The global shortcut opens the panel on the display under the pointer.

  • Leaving

    Esc, or move the pointer away

    Impuls does not become another permanent window: the panel folds back into the edge of the screen and takes no place in application switching.

You can drive the panel from the keyboard, and VoiceOver reads it: every row carries a name, a value and its actions, and every rail icon carries its module's name. Impuls follows the system settings for Reduce Motion, Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency.

Privacy

Your data stays on the Mac

Impuls has no account, advertising, remote configuration or device fingerprinting. Clipboard, notes, snippets, files and calendar go nowhere. The app has three separate network boundaries, and each requires its own action or consent.

  • Update checksImpuls asks on first launch, and you can change the answer later. It reaches only the signed Impuls channel on GitHub. Sparkle's system profiling stays off, and automatic installation is a separate choice again.
  • Web playerChoosing a source in Music makes no request at all. A connection appears only after Open Web Player, and what opens is the selected service's official site in a system WebKit window.
  • Version statisticsOff until a separate opt-in. At most once an hour it sends a random installation pseudonym and the Impuls version, plus a correctly observed previous version after an update. It sends no app content, name, contact details or hardware identifiers.
  • Local dataClipboard history lives in memory by default. If you turn on persistence, the archive is encrypted with AES-GCM and its key is kept in the macOS Keychain. Concealed password-manager entries never reach the history.
  • FeedbackImpuls composes the report on your Mac and shows it to you in full first. It never uploads it: when you press the button, the text goes to the pasteboard and your browser opens a GitHub form. The report carries no clipboard, notes, file names, calendar data, serial numbers or identifiers.

Install

Installing takes three steps

Impuls is ad-hoc signed and not yet notarized by Apple, so the first launch needs your approval. Later updates install from inside the app through the signed channel.

Download for macOS

  • 01

    Download and move it

    Open Impuls-1.4.13.dmg and drag Impuls into Applications.

  • 02

    Allow the first launch

    If macOS refuses to open it, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway. This is needed once.

  • 03

    Set it up

    Pick your shortcut, the panel size, and which modules you want and in what order. Update checks and Apple device discovery are switched on separately.

Questions

Do I need a MacBook with a notch?
No. On a MacBook with a cutout the panel uses its geometry; on any other screen Impuls draws a compact anchor at the top edge. It works on the built-in display, on an external monitor and on an iPad running as a Sidecar display.
Does my data go to the internet?
Clipboard, notes, snippets, files and calendar stay on the Mac. Update checks and the web player are enabled separately. A third separate switch can allow version statistics: a random installation pseudonym and the Impuls version, with no app content, name, contact details or hardware identifiers.
What does it cost?
Nothing. Impuls is free, open source under GPL-3.0-or-later, and needs no account.
Why does macOS complain on first launch?
The build is ad-hoc signed and not yet notarized by Apple, and notarizing it needs a Developer ID. The first launch goes through System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. After that Impuls updates itself through a signed channel and checks the signature before unpacking.
Why are some Battery values missing?
Impuls shows only what macOS publishes about that particular Mac. Temperature, cycles, full capacity and connector type are missing on some machines. Rather than invent a value, the panel leaves it unavailable, which is more use to you than a plausible zero.
How does Impuls see my iPhone and iPad?
Through the trust the device has already given this Mac: over USB, or through Finder Wi-Fi sync. No pairing is created, no local network is scanned, and there is no direct connection to the device. Discovery is off by default, and iPhone and iPad support is marked Beta.
What permissions does it ask for?
Calendar, to show upcoming meetings, and Automation for Apple Music, to read the track title. Both are requested by the standard macOS dialog and are needed only by those modules. Everything else works without them.
Can I move my setup to another Mac?
Yes. Settings, snippets and notes export to a local JSON file and import back. Clipboard history is deliberately not part of a backup.

Try it on your own Mac

Free, no account, no commitment. If it does not suit you, drag it to the Trash and it is gone.
